messages:
Maya (support): FYI ACME is seeing p99s spike to ~6.2s on our text-gen endpoint since ~09:10 UTC. They shared a few request_ids. customer impact: interactive UI freezes.
Ryan (eng-runtime): thanks — can you drop one request_id and a minimal curl to repro? also which model/route are they hitting?
Maya (support): sample id: rq_12987. Route: /v1/generate model=redwood-alpha-16k, tenancy=acme-prod. curl:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":128}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Logs attached from customer show long wait in gateway: "waiting for worker" lines.
Sasha (eng-sre): seeing ingress queue depth spike for tenant acme-prod around 09:08 — worker-pool-3 CPU at 95% and KV cache eviction rising. p95 latency climbed first, then p99. Looks like a small set of heavy requests caused pileup.
Ryan (eng-runtime): pulling metrics now — attaching quick snippet:
```
time, queue_depth, inflight, p95_ms, p99_ms
09:05, 12, 8, 420, 780
09:08, 38, 32, 950, 6200
09:12, 5, 3, 210, 320
```
Ryan (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: a few large-memory prompts caused model instances to block (KV cache thrashing) and admission controller kept allowing requests -> worker saturation.
Sasha (eng-sre): Agreed. Short-term mitigations: 1) route acme-prod to fallback model variant with lower memory (alpha-8k) 2) temporarily lower per-tenant concurrency limit for acme-prod 3) scale up worker-pool-3 by +2 nodes if capacity available. Which do you want applied now?
Ryan (eng-runtime): do 1 + 2 immediately. I'll open a hotpatch to the admission controller to reduce tenant concurrency from 40 -> 12 for acme-prod and add a routing override.
Ryan (eng-runtime): running command to apply routing override:
```
# apply routing override to prefer alpha-8k for acme-prod
redwoodctl routing set --tenant acme-prod --route /v1/generate --prefer-model redwood-alpha-8k --reason "hotfix ingress pileup"
```
InfraBot: routing override created (id: ro_778). Propagating to edge nodes (ETA ~15s).
Ryan (eng-runtime): patching admission controller:
```
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap admission-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"tenants.acme-prod.max_concurrency":"12"}}'
```
InfraBot: admission config reload succeeded on 6/6 controller instances.
Sasha (eng-sre): scaled worker-pool-3 +2 nodes as precaution (auto-scaling failed to trigger due to quota). Nodes are up. Monitoring queue depth.
Leo (customer-success): I'm messaging ACME with an interim note: we routed some traffic to a lower-memory variant to stabilize latency, expecting p99 to drop within 2 minutes. ETA for full fix?
Ryan (eng-runtime): monitoring — p99 dropped from 6.2s -> ~380ms within 90s after routing change and concurrency cap. Will keep an eye for regressions.
Maya (support): customer confirmed improved responsiveness. They saw UI unfreeze. :relieved: Thanks team.
Sasha (eng-sre): follow-ups: 1) add a safer default per-tenant concurrency cap for new tenants 2) add an alert when KV cache eviction > 70% for any worker-pool 3) bake a routing fallback policy into the rollout playbook. I'll create tickets.
Ryan (eng-runtime): also adding a small admission-controller change: if queue depth > 30 && inflight/worker > 0.8, temporarily reject non-interactive batch requests first. Will experiment in canary.
Maya (support): filing this as a Sev3 -> root-cause follow-up, including customer repro steps and our mitigation timeline.
Leo (customer-success): logging follow-up with ACME: timeline and what we changed, thanks.
Ryan (eng-runtime): closing the hotfix PR once canary has 30m stable metrics. Will update thread.
Maya (support): thanks all, resolving on our side for now.
